subject: Novacart — post-incident closure cadence & ownership
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@novacart.com>, ops@novacart.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novacart incident — RCA deliverable & next steps

Ethan / NovaCart ops team,

Thanks again for the bridge yesterday. Attached is Redwood's initial RCA (PDF) covering the 2027-05-02 throughput surge that caused elevated token latency and a spike in 5xx errors for your inference endpoints. High-level summary:

- Root cause: a combination of a model shard rebalance triggered by an autoscaler edge-case and concurrent long-sequence requests that caused KV cache thrashing on our dedicated pool.
- Impact window: 2027-05-02 14:06–14:42 UTC.
- Observed: median token latency increased from ~80ms to ~420ms; error rate peaked at 6.8% for your tenant; tail p95/p99 inflated as batching backpressure accumulated.

Action items in the attached tracker (CSV) are our recommended mitigations and owners. I pulled out the highest-priority corrective items below so we can align on owners and dates for exec reporting:

1) Immediate mitigation (owner: Marcus Lin) — pin model variant to the cold-start-stable build and disable the autoscaler shard rebalance for Novacart's Dedicated pool. Target: 2027-05-04 04:00 UTC.
2) Cache hardening (owner: Laura Bennett) — implement prefix-preserving KV cache guard and add an early abort for >8k token requests that would bypass the cache. Target: 2027-05-10.
3) Rate shaping & circuit (owner: Redwood runtime) — introduce a per-tenant continuous-batching threshold and a soft-circuit to bleed long-running streams during sustained high concurrency. Target: 2027-05-14.
4) Postmortem & exec readout (owner: Kimberly Park) — 10-min exec readout with NovaCart C-suite on 2027-05-07; written summary to be shared 24 hours prior.

Can you confirm: 1) the receipt of the RCA and tracker, 2) whether those owners are OK from your side, and 3) availability for the 2027-05-07 executive readout window (I propose 16:00–16:30 PT)?

Attachments: novacart_incident_rca_v1.pdf, novacart_action_tracker.csv

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

Company: Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@novacart.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@novacart.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novacart incident — RCA deliverable & next steps

Kimberly,

Received — thanks for the fast turnaround and the level of detail. High-level acknowledgement from our side: the timeline and symptom set match what we saw.

We broadly agree with the recommended mitigations. A couple of quick notes/questions:

- For item #1, disabling the rebalance is fine as an immediate stop-gap; we need an ETA on when you expect the Dedicated autoscaler fix to be fully validated.
- For item #2, the abort threshold is useful but NovaCart has a small percentage of valid >8k token jobs for batch analytics. Can we gate the abort to a request-level flag so we don't break those?

We're OK for the executive readout on 2027-05-07 at 16:00 PT. I'll add our CTO and Head of Ops if that's acceptable.

Ethan
Ethan Liu
VP Engineering — NovaCart
ethan.liu@novacart.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@novacart.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novacart incident — RCA deliverable & next steps

Ethan — quick follow-up with more granular owners and a run-of-show for the exec readout.

Per-item owner clarifications (from Redwood):
- Marcus Lin (runtime lead): implement the autoscaler-disable toggle for Novacart and validate no capacity regression. ETA: 2027-05-04 05:00 UTC (slipped from prior but verified window).
- Marcus + Runtime QA: smoke validation & load sanity for pinned variant. ETA: 2027-05-04 10:00 UTC.
- Laura Bennett (platform reliability): implement the KV cache guard and request flag gating for long-sequence analytics jobs. We will add an "analytics_long_run=true" header that bypasses the early-abort logic; tech note will be in the tracker. ETA: 2027-05-11.
- Kimberly Park: prepare exec brief + single-slide incident summary. Draft to be shared by 2027-05-06 16:00 PT.

Exec readout run-of-show (2027-05-07, 16:00 PT, 30 mins):
0–5m: Kimberly — summary + impact metrics (p95/p99, error curve)
5–12m: Marcus — technical root cause and immediate mitigations done
12–22m: Laura — medium-term fixes (cache, gating) + rollout plan
22–28m: Q+A (NovaCart + Redwood eng leads)
28–30m: Next steps and SLA remediation commitments

I'll update the shared tracker and mark statuses after each change.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@novacart.com>, ops@novacart.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novacart incident — RCA deliverable & next steps

Quick status update from runtime:

- Autoscaler rebalance toggle applied to Novacart Dedicated pool at 2027-05-04 05:07 UTC. Observed immediate stabilization; error rate dropped back to baseline within ~18 minutes.
- Pinned model variant deployed and validated under 10k synthetic requests (concurrency sweep). No capacity regression observed.
- Added a telemetry flag (novacart.edge.rebalance_disabled=true) to help post-change monitoring.

Next: I will push the KV cache guard branch to staging today and open a small Gate PR for Laura to review the request-level "analytics_long_run" header behavior. Target rolling to canary by 2027-05-09.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@novacart.com>, Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@novacart.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Novacart incident — exec readout summary & closure checklist

Ethan / Marta,

Thanks for the time today. As promised, a concise summary of what Redwood completed and the agreed next steps for closure: 

Completed (as of 2027-05-07):
- Immediate: rebalance toggle applied + pinned model variant — confirmed by runtime telemetry and NovaCart ops that call latencies returned to SLA bands.
- Short-term validation: smoke tests and concurrency sweeps passed in canary; no regression observed.

Committed medium-term work and ownership:
- KV cache guard + request-header gating (owner: Laura Bennett) — ETA 2027-05-11.
- Continuous-batching threshold and soft-circuit (owner: Runtime Eng) — ETA 2027-05-14.
- SLA credit & remediation timeline (owner: Customer Success) — Redwood CS to follow up by 2027-05-10 with a formal credit recommendation.

Closure criteria we agreed to track in the action tracker:
1) Deploy cache guard to canary and validate against NovaCart's long-sequence jobs (pass/fail)
2) Deploy batching threshold + soft-circuit to canary; validate error-rate drop under stress
3) Confirm no regression across other tenants after rollouts
4) Finalize postmortem doc (v2) with a short remediation pledge for exec record

Please reply with any edits to the summary. If no edits are received, we'll mark this thread as the canonical closure log and update the shared tracker to "In progress" for the outstanding items.

Thanks again — appreciate the partnership on this.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: novacart_incident_rca_v1.pdf, novacart_action_tracker.csv
